It is unanimous PASS with artifact on the two safety-critical lenses: spec-conformance (spec-conformance-rev, artifact-backed) and failure-recovery (6/6 probes, artifact-backed). The other three candidates are disqualified: gen-sonnet-3 and gen-sonnet-4 each carry a spec-conformance fail at BLOCKER severity (ambiguous-resolve returns the first match -> deletes the wrong irreplaceable media; confirmed in source: -4 line 385 `return movie["id"]`, -5 line 521 `return movie.get("id")`, no uniqueness guard) which halts the gate with no override permitted; gen-sonnet-4 additionally carries a boundaries BLOCKER (reconcile_seerr KeyError crash + plex_items reads Video/Directory but not the standard Plex JSON 'Metadata' key, silently returning zero candidates). gen-opus-2 carries a spec-conformance MAJOR (_plex_base() falls back to hardcoded port 32400 when plex.port is absent â€” spec says 'NOT 32400' â€” and _read_secret swallows FileNotFoundError so a missing secret silently connects to the wrong PMS instead of EXIT_FATAL; confirmed source line 238 `(port or "32400")`), which is not unanimous-pass and routes to Stage 0, not commit. gen-opus-1's only fails are three MINOR defects (concurrency, boundaries, security), each verified bounded and non-data-loss. entry: QUORUM CHECK: confirmed every 'pass' has a real evidence_artifact (no pass downgraded to abstain). No spec-conformance fail (would route Stage 0). No blocker fail (would halt with no override). Therefore commit is permitted without override.

QUORUM: 3 candidates x 4 lenses. Unanimous-pass count = 0 -> no clean commit. Blocker-severity fails = 0 -> override available but DECLINED on principled grounds (verified universal false negative). Decision = route_back to Stage 1, base = gen-opus-1.

SPEC-CONFORMANCE: gen-opus-1 PASS (only valid, machine-parseable JSON; artifact present). gen-sonnet-2 FAIL(major) — plain-text/markdown, json.loads raised JSONDecodeError; self-admitted. gen-sonnet-3 FAIL(major) — same, plain-text/markdown not JSON; self-admitted. Both sonnet fails route their OWN repair to Stage 0 per rule, but neither is advanced.

SPEC-FORMAT AMBIGUITY (Stage-0 follow-up): both sonnet candidates cite tooling friction — StructuredOutput 'solution' is a string field, colliding with the 'valid JSON' acceptance criterion. gen-opus-1 resolved via fenced ```json-in-string (parseable after fence strip). Recommend Stage 0 tighten the deliverable-format criterion to remove the ambiguity for future generations.

CONCURRENCY: gen-sonnet-2 PASS (no mutation, no atomicity overclaim — best on lens; artifact present). gen-opus-1 FAIL(minor) — ASSUMPTIONS claims 'single ssh session' but 4 separate ssh calls in its own evidence; no mutation, facts stable. gen-sonnet-3 FAIL(major) — PROVEN box mutation: pytest run created .pytest_cache/__pycache__ on disk, violating spec hard constraint 'no repo or live-box mutation at any stage'; self-mischaracterized as read-only; low blast radius (gitignored) but a demonstrated MUST-NOT breach; plus atomicity overclaim (6 probes vs 'one round-trip').

BOUNDARIES (fails ALL three): SHARED verified false negative — FAQ L635/L652 'total concurrent streams'/'if three people are streaming' mislabels the per-user cap (kill_stream.py MAX_STREAMS_PER_USER=4, arbiter-verified) as a global cross-member cap; all candidates correct only the numeral, none flag the scope error. A doc patched per any candidate still misdescribes the mechanism.

BOUNDARIES (gen-opus-1 specific, major): H2 (Home.md L37) / R2 (README.md L42) correct_state '35 apps' leaves the parenthetical '(19 UCC / 5 systemd / 9 cron / 1 library)'=34 unpatched; arbiter-verified truth is 19/6/9/1=35 -> the fix as written yields '35' beside a breakdown summing to 34 (self-introduced off-by-one). gen-sonnet-2 and gen-sonnet-3 both caught the systemd 5->6 correction; gen-opus-1 did not.

BOUNDARIES (shared minor): all three derive Kuma monitor total '49' without reconciling README L44's own 'self-pushed QFlix Reaper monitor + 4 external monitors' clause; 49 may not equal the live total. Keep at minor + live 'manitoba-maint kuma audit' caveat; do not assert 49 as ground truth.

SECURITY: gen-opus-1 PASS (cleanest — no ~/secrets/ reads, single-quoted grep -F patterns neutralize backtick substitution, no mutation/traversal/SSRF; artifact present). gen-sonnet-3 PASS (one secrets read: seerr.port=42011, already spec-disclosed -> no new exposure; artifact present). gen-sonnet-2 FAIL(major) — (a) unescaped backtick inside double-quoted grep pattern in SECRETS-02 evidence.command triggers unintended shell command-substitution on re-execution (reproduced); systemic authoring style; (b) reads & publishes ~/secrets/homarr.port (42006), not spec-disclosed, where 'ss -ltnp' proves the same claim without touching secrets/.

OVERRIDE: none applied. No blocker existed to force a hard route, but the verified universal boundaries false negative (stream-cap per-user vs total) makes an override-to-commit indefensible — it would commit a known, reproduced false negative into member-facing docs.

ROUTE TARGET: Stage 1 (not Stage 0). Advanced candidate gen-opus-1 passes spec-conformance; its blocker is boundaries, a content-repair issue against unambiguous spec ground truth. Repaired deliverable MUST re-enter Stage 2 before commit.

ARBITER VERIFICATION (anti-laundering): independently reproduced kill_stream.py per-user cap=4, FAQ L635/L652 'total concurrent streams'/'three people' framing, and manifest 35 apps + 13 canaries + class breakdown 19/6/9/1 — all confirm the boundaries reviewer's artifacts; the decline-override rests on verified fact, not reviewer consensus.

UNIVERSAL BOUNDARIES FALSE NEGATIVE: no candidate flagged the FAQ stream-cap per-user-vs-total mischaracterization (L635/L652). Unresolved by every candidate; must be generated fresh in Stage 1 and re-reviewed in Stage 2.

SPEC-FORMAT / TOOLING AMBIGUITY: 'valid JSON' acceptance criterion vs StructuredOutput string-only 'solution' channel tripped 2 of 3 generators. gen-opus-1 satisfied it (fenced JSON), so the CONTENT repair goes to Stage 1 — but the format criterion itself should be pinned in Stage 0 (e.g., 'fenced ```json block, parseable after fence strip') to prevent recurrence.

rationale: ROUTE_BACK to Stage 1. Gate math: COMMIT requires unanimous pass across all five active lenses (spec-conformance, concurrency, boundaries, security, failure-recovery) or a logged arbiter override. No candidate is unanimous — concurrency-rev fails all three (major), failure-recovery-rev fails both COMMIT candidates (major, having falsified their 'not persistently masked' Q1 rulings). No fail carries blocker severity and no enumerated hard-blocker trigger is met (re-verified in source), so the no-override rule is not engaged; override is theoretically available but I decline it. The two decisive defects are masked live-write FAILURES on a paying Sonarr/Radarr stack, not doc/count/observability gaps that 'cannot cause a wrong live write,' so they fail the spec's own override-eligibility test:

entry: D1 (major, spec-conformance/failure-recovery, VERIFIED at specials_policy.py:95-113): per-series GET /episode failure swallowed as eps=[]; S0 season-flag PUT still fires (two-step write decoupled) and status stays 'ok'. Transient=convergent; PERSISTENT failure => series permanently skipped from run 2 (flag reads cleared, mon_ids empty), S0 episodes left monitored, no error surfaced, main --cron exit 0/Kuma green. Under-implements design's 'error-level on API failure.' Fix: gen-sonnet-3 split-status patch.

D2 (major, concurrency/failure-recovery, VERIFIED at quality_fallback.py:282-286,473-477,510): plan_tv sets rec['parked']=True in persisted state BEFORE _apply_tv_park is confirmed; run() saves state unconditionally with no rollback on ok=False; park is once-only so a single failed unmonitor permanently forecloses retry — episode stays monitored/unfindable while state records 'parked.' Centerpiece new live-write path of Component B; surfaced by NO candidate. Mitigation is only a one-shot Discord error notify.

D3 (major, failure-recovery, VERIFIED at quality_fallback.py:476,544-546): main() exit-code inspects only res['per_arr'] (movies); a failed TV park lives in res['tv_parks'] and never sets exit 1 => Kuma/systemd_oneshot stay green despite a failed live write. Compounds D2.

D4 (minor/pre-existing, concurrency): state.json read-modify-write is unguarded (no lock/CAS); overlapping quality_fallback runs can lose day counters. Safe direction (resets counters), load_state/save_state byte-unchanged; asserted-not-tested by the COMMIT candidates.

D5 (latent, boundaries, VERIFIED at specials_policy.py:95,109): a series dict missing 'id' raises an uncaught KeyError that crashes the entire run() — sonarr2 is never attempted (no per-instance exception isolation). Requires non-stock payload; flag for Stage-1 hardening.
D6 (informational, boundaries): seasonNumber excluded via Python == (int); a string '0' season would not be excluded. Real Sonarr always sends int.

D7 / Q2 (informational, boundaries, VERIFIED at specials_policy.py:74-75): _with_season0_unmonitored writes monitored=None for any non-S0 season lacking a 'monitored' key. Stock Sonarr 4.0.17 always emits the boolean, so no real repro; cheap defensive fix s.get('monitored', True) recommended before long-term trust.

D8 / Q3 (deploy precondition): PUT /series/{id} full-object round-trip fidelity vs the real Sonarr 4.0.17 validator is unverifiable in the faked suite (fakes echo the body). MANDATORY operator dry-run / single manual PUT before the first 06:00 live fire — not a static-suite pass.

D9 (evidence-fidelity, non-code): gen-opus-1 and gen-sonnet-3 both describe calling main(['--cron']) and reading an int, which TypeErrors against the real zero-arg main() signature; that specific exit-contract evidence is not reproducible as written. gen-opus-2 tested it correctly via sys.argv monkeypatch (the underlying contract holds).

D10 (candidate-reasoning defect): gen-opus-1/gen-opus-2 COMMIT rulings assert Q1 is 'not persistently masked'; failure-recovery-rev falsified this with a persistent-failure repro. Their COMMIT rests partly on an incorrect convergence claim.
OVERRIDE: none issued. Override was available (no blocker) but declined — D1/D2/D3 are masked live-write failures on a paying stack, not override-eligible 'cannot-cause-a-wrong-live-write' gaps.

ROUTING: Stage 1 (implementation), not Stage 0 — design intent is sound; code under-implements failure surfacing (D1) and write-confirmation (D2/D3). Any Stage-1 fix MUST re-enter Stage 2 before re-arbitration; never commit the un-reviewed patched merge.

entry: DEFECT (observability, non-blocking) D1 info-notify suppression: specials_policy.main() gates the operator info-notify on per-INSTANCE status=='ok', so under a 'partial-episode-fetch-failure' instance a genuinely-enforced sibling series' 'what got cleaned' summary is dropped while the error line + --cron exit 1 (Kuma red) still fire. Write lands and appears in the JSON changes[]; not a masked-live-write. Reproduced across spec-conformance, failure-recovery, boundaries. Spec pre-classified as observability -> does not force route-back. Stage-1 follow-up candidate: surface per-series changes[] even under partial status.

DEFECT (failure-recovery/observability granularity, non-blocking) Within-instance exception audit-loss: a later malformed series (missing 'id' -> KeyError) inside enforce_instance's loop makes run()'s per-instance try/except mark the WHOLE instance 'failed-exception', discarding changes/series_changed/episodes_unmonitored detail for an EARLIER series in the same loop whose /episode/monitor + /series PUTs already landed. Status stays non-ok/red (never masked-green). D5 isolation is instance-level, not series-level. Found by gen-sonnet-3, reproduced by failure-recovery FR-3 and boundaries. Non-blocking; follow-up ticket.

DEFECT (concurrency, pre-existing/out-of-scope, non-blocking BUT deploy-note correction required) D4 severity sharpened: save_state()'s shared, unlocked tmp filename under overlapping qf.run() invocations yields a reachable UNCAUGHT OSError and, in 2 of ~12 trials, a FULL state.json reset (all movie+TV records lost, silently absorbed by load_state's blanket except-pass). This is materially worse than the spec's assumed 'fails safe (counter reset)' and than gen-sonnet-4's 'never a wrong write, only a delayed promotion/park.' Never produced a masked-green outcome (parked=True never survives a failed write). Not introduced by 5c2ff5f; outside AC-17 static gate -> not a route-back trigger. Remediation: add a state.json lockfile before any overlapping cron cadence; correct the operator-facing 'fails safe' language.

DEFECT (diagnosability, new surface, non-blocking) D5 bare `except Exception` retains only str(e)[:300], no traceback; genuinely NEW surface per git diff 55eda48..5c2ff5f. Correctly isolates instances and drives non-ok/exit-1, but an operator gets a one-line truncated string in Kuma/Discord with no traceback. Flagged by gen-sonnet-4 and security/boundaries notes.

DEFECT (candidate risk-framing inaccuracy, not a code defect) gen-opus-1, gen-opus-2, gen-sonnet-4 claim *arr error text (potentially API-key-in-URL) could reach a Discord notify; security lens disproved on two grounds: --cron notify carries only the slug list (never str(e)); API key travels only via X-Api-Key header, never the URL; ArrClient swallows transport exceptions into status-0 tuples before they reach run()'s try/except. Overstated hypothetical in the conservative direction -> non-blocking, but the write-up is inaccurate and should be corrected.

EVIDENCE GAP (non-blocking) gen-sonnet-3 has no security-labeled RISKS entry -> zero security-lens self-assessment for this re-review; independent security probes found nothing to route back on, but this seat's security evidence base is empty.

PROCESS (non-blocking) Artifact portability: all four candidate repro scripts hardcode paths to now-deleted ephemeral worktrees / session scratchpaths; they were genuinely executed at generation time (reviewers re-ran patched copies and reproduced identical output: 42/42, 42/42, 42/0-failed, 14/14). Not portable as-is; non-discriminating across candidates.

PROCESS (test-harness hygiene, non-blocking) notify.log pollution: dry_run=False repro runs invoked the real lib.notify.notify() and wrote to the live ~/.opt/maint/notify.log / notify-fail.log when MANITOBA_STATE_DIR was unset; gen-sonnet-3 disclosed and self-remediated its own byte-matched lines. Future repro harnesses MUST set an isolated MANITOBA_STATE_DIR (mirror the suite's _isolate_notify()).

DEPLOY GATE (carried forward, MANDATORY) D8: real Sonarr 4.0.17.2952 PUT /series full-object validator fidelity is unverifiable against echoing fakes. Before first live fire the operator MUST run one single real PUT /series/{id} dry probe against a benign series and confirm the full-object body round-trips (S0 flag flips, non-S0 flags preserved, no dropped/rejected fields). A green static suite does NOT prove the live PUT lands. Deploy precondition attached to the COMMIT; not itself a route-back trigger.

GATE RESULT: suite 881 passed / 5 skipped confirmed live across seats; AC-11 file scope (exactly 5 files) and byte-unchanged movie logic confirmed via git show --stat / git diff hunk headers; D1/D2/D3/D5/D7 each independently verified resolved by executable artifact; all original invariants (janitor S0-only scope, park guards, MAX_TV_PARKS_PER_RUN=10 overflow-deferred, no TV quality-profile write, correct v3 payloads, dry_run == zero writes + zero state mutation) intact. No residual masked-live-write and no new fix-introduced defect. No arbiter override exercised (unanimous pass with artifacts).

Concurrency lens vs. spec assumption + adopted writeup: the concurrency artifact (full state.json loss under concurrent save_state) materially contradicts the spec's D4 'fails safe (counter reset)' framing and every candidate's deploy-note language (gen-sonnet-4's 'never a wrong write, only a delayed promotion/park' is the sharpest overclaim; gen-opus-2's 'fails safe (counter reset / next-run retry)' also undersells it). Does NOT flip the gate (pre-existing, out of static scope, never masked-green), but no candidate's operator-facing characterization of D4 is correct. The adopted writeup's deploy note MUST be amended and a state.json lockfile added before overlapping cron cadences are tightened.

Residual live-write uncertainty: the entire COMMIT rests on echoing fakes; D8 (real-Sonarr full-object PUT acceptance) is structurally unverifiable in-suite and is closed ONLY by the attached operator single-PUT dry-run gate. Spec sanctions the fakes, so this is not a route-back, but the COMMIT is conditional -- if the D8 gate is skipped, the very first live run could reveal a masked-write this review cannot catch.
